question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No. (iii).
solution:
The correct answer is '**whisked**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passage describes a quick, almost seamless action taken by Secret Service Agents.
 
• The appropriate verb should convey the promptness and urgency of moving President Ronald Reagan to safety.
 
• "**Whisked**" fits well as it conveys the sense of moving someone quickly and smoothly, which is fitting for the context of Secret Service Agents responding rapidly.
 
• Other options ("**pulled**", "**pushed**", "**called**") do not accurately capture the urgency and smoothness needed in the context.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 1**'.

 

Complete Passage: *On the afternoon of 30 March 1981, many Americans experienced a 1. feeling__ of déjà-vu. Déjà-vu is a name given to the feeling that a person has seen or experienced an event before. Many Americans could not help having that feeling on this day. The 2. __news__ hit TVs and radios immediately. President Ronald Reagan had been shot. He was leaving a hotel in Washington DC, turned to wave at some of the people gathered to see him, and fell towards the ground. Before he could hit the ground, his Secret Service Agents 3. __whisked__ him into the car and rushed to the nearest hospital. This same story had been heard before. On 22 November 1963 President John F Kennedy was riding in a motorcade through Dallas, Texas. He smiled and waved to the crowd that had gathered to see him. 4. ________ rang out from a nearby building. The President collapsed into the backseat of the car and was immediately taken to the nearest hospital. He was 5. **________ **dead at the hospital. Now, just seventeen years later, the news sounded eerily the same.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Pulled** (खींचा): "Pulled" suggests a forceful action that could imply a level of struggle or difficulty, which is not fitting for the smooth and quick transport of the President.
 
• **Pushed** (धक्का दिया): "Pushed" indicates moving someone with force, generally in a forward motion, which doesn't align with the context of being quickly moved into a car.
 
• **Called** (बुलाया): "Called" means to summon, which does not fit the context of physically moving someone quickly to safety.
